title: QUIC RFC 9000 CONNECTION_CLOSE Frame Focused Proof
purpose: Describe the focused proof boundary for RFC 9000 CONNECTION_CLOSE frame parsing, formatting, reason-phrase bounds, application-close packet-space constraints, and handshake-abandon transport-close behavior.
design_summary: The proof stays on the existing immutable frame model, frame codec, packet classifier, and local-close runtime seams. Transport CONNECTION_CLOSE frames carry type 0x1c, error code, triggering frame type, reason length, and reason bytes. Application CONNECTION_CLOSE frames carry type 0x1d, error code, reason length, and reason bytes while omitting the triggering frame type. Packet-space tests prove application-specific close payloads are only classified in application-data packets, and runtime tests prove handshake-abandon close uses the transport close variant with APPLICATION_ERROR.
data_and_state_considerations: The frame codec preserves variable-length integer encodings for error code, triggering frame type, and reason length while rejecting truncated fields and overlong reason declarations. Reason bytes remain opaque at the codec boundary, allowing UTF-8 reason phrases without rejecting malformed bytes. Packet-size limits are represented by formatter destination-buffer checks because the frame is serialized atomically into a single buffer.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Type values outside 0x1c and 0x1d, including non-minimal varint encodings of those values, are rejected by the focused parser proof.
Application-specific close frames omit the triggering frame type and are shorter than equivalent transport close frames.
Unknown triggering frame type is represented as 0, matching the PADDING-frame sentinel.
Zero-length reason phrases and malformed UTF-8 reason bytes are preserved rather than treated as parser errors.
The handshake-abandon proof covers the permitted Initial or Handshake transport-close form, not an application-close payload in those spaces.
alternatives_considered: Keep broad QuicFrameCodec and runtime close tests as the only proof; rejected because live triage requires direct requirement-home evidence for S19P19.
Fold HANDSHAKE_DONE and registry/security error-code cleanup into this slice; rejected because S19P20 and S21 have separate remaining blockers.
Add new production error-code validation for all application protocols; rejected because S19P19 only distinguishes the QUIC transport code space from application-defined codes at the frame boundary.
risks: This proof does not claim complete close retransmission, drain timing, or packet coalescing behavior.
This proof does not close the remaining S19P20 or S21 registry/security requirements in the same generated chunk.
Fuzz coverage for this frame family remains deferred in the requirement metadata where the authored coverage expectation says so.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers focused S19P19 CONNECTION_CLOSE parser, formatter, packet-space, and handshake-abandon proof only.
